root_selected_source_scope.scope: Only original Theorem 1 is selected: every positive modulus, a sufficiently high distinct-wise intersection requirement depending on that modulus, every positive ground-set size, the exact additive constant, and its disappearance for sufficiently large divisible sizes. The full authored small-doubling theorem with all three fully editable matrix illustrations, prime-power lifting, repeated squaring, atomic closed-family theorem, Oddtown variant, matching removal and main closing are included. Ordinary prerequisites are basic linear algebra over finite fields/modular rings, elementary prime-power congruences, and Odlyzko [17] Boolean-points bound stated as Lemma 14. Freiman/Ruzsa approximate-group references in the introduction are positioning only and are not proof prerequisites. Source statement/proof literals such as the scalar count d-h in Lemma 11, the base-case product notation and the unprimed S/A-prime construction at main closing are preserved unchanged. Unselected stability and dimension variants are not counted; their omitted counters are restored so all original selected indices remain exact.
root_selected_source_scope.reason: After ordinary finite-dimensional linear algebra and the named Boolean-points rank bound, the human proof still constructs disjoint-support coordinatewise products to isolate a low-dimensional exceptional coordinate set. Repeated doubling and prime-power lifts must then force large twin atoms of the prescribed modulus, followed by an exact matching-removal argument and atomic closing that improves a linear exceptional error to a constant. These coupled structural steps exceed routine qualification linear algebra or inclusion-exclusion, so the original primary result is conservatively H1.
